reference: Dempster, Petitjean and Webb (2020), ROCKET: Exceptionally fast and accurate time series classification using random convolutional kernels, Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 34:1454–1495. DOI 10.1007/s10618-020-00701-z; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.13051. Read original manuscript sections 3–3.4, pages 5–9, not entire paper. Random Gaussian mean-centered kernels vary length, dilation, padding and bias; each returns PPV and maximum. Default 10,000 kernels give 20,000 features; a ridge classifier chooses regularization using efficient training cross-validation. This supports a published-method transfer baseline, not originality or expected accuracy improvement. The aeon multivariate channel sampling, per-channel normalization and current sklearn pipeline are explicit library adaptations, not an exact original univariate experiment replication. Its classifier citation has the correct authors; the transform docstring incorrectly lists MultiRocket authors, so we use the paper author list. No new method contribution established.
